title: Storage guardrail Terraform module: EBS/EFS/S3 defaults and health probes
creator: Priya Sharma
description: Create a reusable Terraform module that centralizes storage guardrails for Private (VPC) deployments. The module will provision and configure EBS, EFS, and S3 primitives with secure defaults, KMS key provisioning and rotation support, automated snapshot/backup tagging, and lightweight health probes to surface configuration and retention drift. This module is meant for use in our private control plane and on-prem Terraform stacks and should make upgrades safe across TF and provider versions.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes inputs to enable/disable enforcement for each storage type (ebs_enforce, efs_enforce, s3_enforce).

Default encryption enforced: EBS volumes use a provided KMS key or create one with alias (redwood/storage/{{env}}), EFS created with kms_key_id when encryption in transit/at-rest enabled, S3 buckets default to kms-managed encryption with enforced bucket policy.
Snapshots/backups created by the module are tagged with environment, team, cost-center, and retention_policy metadata.

A scheduled health probe (Lambda + CloudWatch Event or native SSM Automation) validates: latest snapshot age <= configured threshold, S3 lifecycle rules present for infrequent access/archive, EFS lifecycle policy applied, and no unencrypted buckets/volumes exist.
Module provides an output that summarizes potential driftable items and a `health_check_report` S3 object location when run in CI.
Terraform plan/apply for an existing stack with module v0.0.X -> v1.0.0 performs non-destructive changes by default and documents necessary manual steps if any destructive action is required.
Automated unit and integration tests in CI (terraform-compliance + real AWS acceptance run in dedicated infra account) pass and are included in PR pipeline.
tasks: Draft module public interface (inputs/outputs) and default values
Implement KMS provisioning pattern with optional customer-managed key input
Implement EBS defaults: gp3, encrypted=true, deletion_snapshot=false toggle
Implement EFS defaults: encrypted=true, lifecycle policy input, performance mode input
Implement S3 defaults: block public access, default encryption using kms_alias, lifecycle rules, bucket logging option
Add snapshot tagging and retention configuration for EBS/EFS backup jobs
Create lightweight health probe (Lambda) + CloudWatch metric and dashboard
Add terraform upgrade guide and migration helper scripts for v0.x -> v1.x
Write CI acceptance tests and run in infra-integration account
Create docs (Confluence and examples) and a consuming-stack example for private deploy
decision_log: 2026-03-06: Chosen pattern: module will create a default KMS key when kms_key_id not provided to avoid manual provisioning for smaller customers. Alias pattern set to alias/redwood/storage-{env}.
2026-03-07: Decided against forcing deletion snapshots by default to avoid accidental cost and data loss; instead provide a 'create_snapshot_before_delete' flag for destructive operations.
2026-03-09: Health probe implemented as Lambda + CloudWatch Event for immediate observability; also expose a terraform-only 'dry_run_health_check' flag for CI checks.
2026-03-11: Upgrade strategy: bump module major when any resource schema change would force replacement; include migration guide and an automated lint that detects replacement-risk changes in PRs.
notes: Avoid complex cross-account snapshot sharing in v1: this adds policy surface and will be a follow-up once org-level snapshot policies are validated.
S3 bucket ownership enforcement: require bucket_owner_full_control ACL on replication targets for any cross-account replication configured by customers.
We will default to AWS-managed rotation for KMS but enable key rotation for customer keys when created by the module.

Module should be provider-agnostic where possible but will use aws provider features that require aws >= 4.x; include provider version constraint and migration notes for provider v5+ where breaking changes exist.
progress_updates: 2026-03-06: Interface sketch completed and reviewed with Platform PM. Added inputs for enforcement toggles and retention windows.
2026-03-08: Initial KMS provisioning and EBS resource templates implemented. Ran local terraform plan against dev account; surfaced required IAM permissions.
2026-03-10: Health probe Lambda skeleton completed and test harness added. Discovered edge case: snapshots created outside module need tagging reconciler job.
2026-03-13: CI tests wired up to run acceptance tests in infra-integration; two failing tests related to s3 bucket policy ordering fixed.
qa_plan: Unit tests: terraform fmt & validate, tflint rules for module conventions
Integration: spin up module in infra-integration account with minimal and strict configs; verify resources, encryption, tags, lifecycle rules
Health tests: execute Lambda probe and assert CloudWatch metric emits expected state; confirm health report written to S3
Upgrade test: run terraform plan/apply using existing stacks and simulate v0.x -> v1.0 upgrade path in a sandbox account
Security: run static scan for IAM policy least-privilege and request security review (security_review_required=true)
rollback_plan: If deploy introduces replacement-causing changes: immediately abort and apply previous module version pinned in Terraform statefile;
If probes misreport or cause noise: disable health_probe via module input and revert probe Lambda to previous version
If KMS key creation conflicts with customer-managed keys: remove module-created key and re-run with kms_key_id provided by customer
release_plan: Cut v1.0.0 release with changelog and migration guide
Publish module to internal registry and update consuming stacks to pin to v1.0.0 in a canary environment
Monitor infra-integration dashboards for 72 hours for snapshot/retention drift alerts
Run post-release retrospective and capture follow-ups into ENG backlog
implementation_notes: Keep resources optional and non-destructive by default. Use data resources to detect pre-existing unencrypted items and report them rather than forcibly re-creating. Prefer small, composable submodules (kms, ebs_defaults, efs_defaults, s3_guardrail, health_probe) so teams can import only what they need.
example_usage:
module "storage_guardrail" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood-inference/infra.git//modules/storage-guardrail?ref=v1.0.0"
  env = "prod"
  ebs_enforce = true
  s3_enforce = true
  kms_key_alias = "alias/redwood/storage-prod"
  create_health_probe = true
}
